name: AARP and All Our Ideas: Using Wiki Surveys for Identifying Problems at Scale (Briefing Note)
content:
## AARP and All Our Ideas: Using Wiki Surveys for Identifying Problems at Scale

**Owner:** AARP and The Governance Lab
**Location:** USA
**Years in Operation:** 2019-present
**Implementation Level:** National
**Platforms:** Web
**Method:** Pairwise wikisurveys (AllOurIdeas)
**Participatory Task:** Opinions

### Overview
AARP, the nation's largest nonprofit, and The Governance Lab (The GovLab) launched an online consultation to better understand AARP members' concerns about 'big health data.' They used a wiki survey tool, which tabulates the inputs even of tens of thousands of people without the need for those running the consultation to do extra work to extract meaning from citizen responses.

### How It Works
Big health data refers to the ability to gather and analyze large quantities of information about health, wellness and lifestyle, including data from health care providers and apps that track sleep, exercise habits, and purchases. AARP and the GovLab used All Our Ideas — a 'wiki survey' tool developed by researchers at Princeton University — to gauge AARP members' concerns on which big health data issues were most important to them.

Rather than give respondents a lengthy survey, the wiki survey presents participants with two randomly selected items and asks them to select the one of greater concern. The GovLab and AARP prepared 63 statements such as 'Big health data may lead to the encouragement of self-diagnosis over seeing a doctor.' Respondents answer as many or as few randomized pairings as they want and may also submit their own answer choices.

### Participation
Voting remained open for three weeks in December 2019 and over 5,000 participants cast 67,000 votes. No demographic information was collected about respondents.

### Results
At the end of the consultation, AARP received a rank ordered list of problems. Participants articulated that ensuring corporate accountability and preventing discrimination by insurers were their most pressing concerns regarding the use of their health data. AARP used the findings from the wiki survey to run a second consultation, asking people to identify novel solutions to the problems identified via All Our Ideas.

### Cost
All Our Ideas is a free, open source tool available at allourideas.org. Anyone can set up a wiki survey on the All Our Ideas website. The public version of the tool can be embedded in any website at no cost and with basic knowledge of HTML/CSS.
